title: Yield Relationships & Bond Math

sections.heading: The 4 Yields — Definitions
items: Nominal (Coupon/Stated) Yield: FIXED % of par set at issue. 6% coupon = $60/yr forever, regardless of price.
Current Yield (CY): Annual coupon ÷ Current market price. Ignores gain/loss at maturity.
Yield to Maturity (YTM): Annualized total return if held to maturity. Includes coupon + discount gain OR – premium loss. Also called the bond's 'basis'.
Yield to Call (YTC): Same as YTM but uses call date & call price. Accelerates the discount gain OR premium loss into a shorter time frame.

items.Logic: Earlier call accelerates the discount GAIN
Earlier call accelerates the premium LOSS

sections.heading: Key Formulas
items: Current Yield = Annual Coupon ÷ Market Price
Tax-Equivalent Yield (TEY) = Muni Yield ÷ (1 − Tax Bracket)
Muni-Equivalent Yield = Corp Yield × (1 − Tax Bracket)
Bond Price ($) = Quoted Price × 10  (e.g., quote of 97.5 = $975)
Inverse Rule: Interest rates ↑ → Bond prices ↓ (and vice versa)

sections.heading: TEY Worked Example
items: Investor in 30% bracket, muni yields 7%: TEY = 7% ÷ (1 − 0.30) = 7% ÷ 0.70 = 10%
Corp must yield >10% to beat the muni after tax
Higher tax bracket = greater muni advantage

sections.heading: YTC vs YTM — When Each Is Worse
items: PREMIUM bond: YTC is the WORST yield (lowest) — assume issuer calls when rates fall → investor loses premium faster. Quote YTC.
DISCOUNT bond: YTM is the WORST yield (lowest) — issuer unlikely to call; investor waits longer for gain. Quote YTM.
Rule of thumb: Always quote the LOWER of YTM/YTC to the customer (yield-to-worst).

sections.heading: Quick Recognition Cues
items: 'Trading at 102' → Premium bond ($1,020); coupon is HIGHEST yield
'Trading at 94' → Discount bond ($940); coupon is LOWEST yield
Coupon NEVER changes — only the other 3 yields move with price

common_traps: Confusing POINTS (price, $10) with BASIS POINTS (yield, 0.01%). A bond down 50 bps ≠ down $5.
Forgetting the seesaw flips for premium bonds: at a premium, YTC is LOWEST (not highest) — call accelerates the premium loss.
Applying accrued interest to zero-coupon bonds — they pay NO accrued interest (no current coupon to accrue).
Using corporate yield in the TEY numerator. Formula is MUNI ÷ (1 − bracket); muni yield is always the lower number.
Assuming coupon yield changes when price changes — it NEVER does. Only CY, YTM, and YTC move.
Using T+2 for corporate/muni settlement — the SEC moved to T+1 effective 5/28/2024.
